svg.data-vd-play-label: Play: meiosis I and meiosis II
svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Interphase: DNA replicates, so each chromosome becomes two sister chromatids. The cell is diploid (2n = 4): two homologous pairs."], [3, "Prophase I: chromosomes condense. Homologous chromosomes pair up to form bivalents, and non-sister chromatids cross over at chiasmata, swapping sections of DNA. The nuclear envelope breaks down."], [7, "Metaphase I: bivalents line up on the equator. Which way each pair faces is random (independent assortment), so maternal and paternal chromosomes are mixed in new combinations."], [10, "Anaphase I: homologous chromosomes are pulled to opposite poles; the sister chromatids stay together. This halves the chromosome number."], [13, "Telophase I and cytokinesis: two haploid cells form (n = 2). Each chromosome is still made of two chromatids, which are no longer identical because of crossing over."], [16.5, "Prophase II and metaphase II: in each cell a new spindle forms at right angles to the first, and the chromosomes line up singly on its equator."], [19, "Anaphase II: the centromeres divide and the sister chromatids are pulled to opposite poles."], [22, "Telophase II and cytokinesis: four haploid cells (gametes in animals), each with one chromosome from every pair, and all genetically different from each other and from the parent cell."]]
svg.title: Meiosis in an animal cell
svg.desc: An animated cell with two homologous pairs going through meiosis I and meiosis II, showing pairing, crossing over, independent assortment and the four haploid cells produced.
svg.text: Red chromosomes came from the mother, blue from the father. Watch the colour swap at crossing over.

g.data-info: Divides twice by cytokinesis: meiosis makes four cells from one.
Breaks down before each division and re-forms around each new set of chromosomes.
Microtubules from the poles that attach to the centromeres and pull chromosomes (meiosis I) or chromatids (meiosis II) apart.
Where the bivalents line up in metaphase I (in pairs) and the chromosomes line up in metaphase II (singly).
Red came from the mother, blue from the father. Each was copied in interphase, so at first it is two sister chromatids joined at a centromere.
A point where non-sister chromatids of a homologous pair break and rejoin, exchanging sections: new combinations of alleles.
In prophase I the two homologous chromosomes pair up side by side. Non-sister chromatids can cross over at points called chiasmata, swapping sections of DNA (alleles).

g.text: 2n = 4 → 2 cells, n = 2 → 4 cells, n = 2, all genetically different
